goal: Add a test-only assertion proving manifest telemetry triage.highest_severity is a faithful passthrough of the triage summary highest_severity for a completed triage run with severity-bearing items.
background:
Acceptance criteria:
- internal/manifest/manifest_test.go gains at least one assertion that, for a completed triage run (final.json with status complete and items carrying severity), telemetry.triage.highest_severity equals the highest-ranked severity present in items per the existing high > medium > low > none ordering, and equals the value at the manifest's top-level triage.highest_severity (passthrough).
- The new or extended test seeds at least one item with severity "high" so the asserted value is deterministic, and exercises the fully completed-triage path (final.json present, status complete, fresh input_hashes via triage.ComputeInputHashes, triage.md present).
- All existing tests in ./internal/manifest/... continue to pass. Only test files under internal/manifest/ are touched; no production source files are modified. The telemetry JSON schema (field names, shapes, schema_version) is unchanged.

Existing test TestWriteRunManifestTelemetryTriageStates covers the completed ("yes") triage path but only asserts state and item_count; TestWriteRunManifestMarksZeroSelectedTriage asserts highest_severity == nil only for an empty items array. The passthrough of triage.highest_severity through telemetry.triage.highest_severity for completed triage runs with severity-bearing items is currently unverified. telemetryTriageSummary (internal/manifest/manifest.go) copies triageSummary["highest_severity"]; highestSeverity ranking is high > medium > low > none.
Bakeoff will capture candidate patches from isolated worktrees and will not apply them to this checkout.

build.comparison_goal: Prefer the patch that satisfies the acceptance criteria with the smallest maintainable change.
